Variants.Content: New Ibbish is the island of Ibban and its shipping routes located on the Trembling Sea, and is politically within the Iban island and port system. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry New Ibbish Local families also relied on blubber, fish, furs, hardwoods and the short shipping season; if a road, well or dock failed, the price fell first to them.

Entry New Ibbish New Is is located in the power and trade network of Iban and the Shivering Sea. The rules inside and outside the city gate are determined by the local order; whether the defenders are well fed and whether reinforcements can arrive on time are more important than the rhetoric in the meeting hall in determining whether this stronghold is reliable.

Entry New Ibbish They will also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of Iban and the Shivering Sea; reputations can spread far from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheels, oars, or horse hooves.

Entry New Ibbish New Is is located in the power and trade network of Iban and the Shivering Sea. The rules inside and outside the city gates are determined by the local order; after the flag is changed, the roads, granaries, old debts and local trusts still have to be taken over by the new owners one by one.

Entry New Ibbish If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The traces left by generations of people in New Yis are half hidden in the ship repair wood, canvas, salt, fish catch and stones used to resist the sea wind, and the other half are hidden in the ancestral spirits of the Iban people, the legends of sea beasts and the common taboos of the cold port. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry New Ibbish They care about blubber, fish catches, furs, hardwoods, and the short sailing season. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting food and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
